title: A Tear on Erev Yom Kippur
summary: How long a talmid may leave home to learn, and what it costs the wife who waits. A sigh breaks half the body, yet the Jew walking with a gentile kept his pace. Then Rav Rechumi, who came home once a year on Erev Yom Kippur, until the year he stayed learning and his wife's tear brought down the roof; Yehuda the son of Rabbi Chiya and the pillar of fire; the power of a tzaddik's words, with the Rav's memory of the Rebbe's heart attack for Rosh Chodesh Kislev; and Rebbi's match for his son.
key_ideas: Learning Torah away from home must not come at the expense of one's wife; her tear has great power.
A sigh breaks the body, but a Jew who is used to hardship keeps going.
The words of a tzaddik have the power to bring about what they say, for good even more than for bad.
Be home on the days that matter.
